description: LUNARIS is an independently developed project created by a solo participant. I led the project concept, research, system design, development, and technical decisions, using AI-assisted tools selectively for code review, debugging, and quality assurance.
summary:
LUNARIS is an interactive lunar mission-planning prototype that helps users explore how surface topography and mission timing affect sunlight availability and direct-to-Earth visibility at candidate landing sites.

The application combines a 3D visualization of lunar terrain derived from NASA LOLA elevation data with local-horizon analysis and time-based visualization of the Sun and Earth. Users can select a landing site, specify coordinates, set a UTC date and time, choose an analysis period, and adjust observer height.

By showing how surrounding terrain can obstruct sunlight and the geometric line of sight to Earth, LUNARIS makes complex lunar surface conditions easier to understand and compare.

The project addresses the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge by bringing terrain, celestial geometry, and mission-time controls into one accessible interface. It supports preliminary exploration of illumination conditions and potential direct-to-Earth visibility windows relevant to lunar surface operations.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

LUNARIS is an interactive tool for exploring lunar landing-site conditions. It combines NASA LOLA topographic data, 3D terrain visualization, local-horizon analysis, and time-based visualization of the Sun and Earth.

Users can select a landing site, specify coordinates, choose a UTC date and time, set the analysis period, and adjust observer height. The application visualizes how surrounding terrain may obstruct sunlight and the geometric line of sight to Earth.

What benefits does it have, and what is its intended impact?

LUNARIS makes complex lunar surface conditions easier to understand by connecting topography with celestial geometry. It helps users examine illumination and potential direct-to-Earth visibility windows when exploring candidate landing locations and mission timing.

The intended impact is to make preliminary lunar mission-planning analysis more accessible to researchers, educators, students, and the public.

What makes it creative?

Rather than displaying the Sun and Earth independently of the surface, LUNARIS places their apparent positions in the context of the surrounding 3D lunar terrain, making local topographic obstructions easier to understand.

Programming language: Python.

Application framework: Streamlit.

Scientific data: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) topographic data.

Additional technologies: Custom Python-based terrain processing, local-horizon calculations, time-based visualization, and interactive 3D rendering.

Development and version control: Git and GitHub.
Live App: https://ladymoonweb-lunaris-app-gs0vnh.streamlit.app/

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/LadyMoonWeb/LUNARIS
